evidence.claim: The persisted content types are STORY, MEDITATION, and LULLABY; an audio story is not a separate content type.
Story narration is a story localization property, while page audio belongs to localized story pages; these are distinct from a generic localized audio field.
A localization can manage localized title, description/body, cover asset, duration, and its relevant audio binding.
Content-level metadata includes external key, age range, and active state; content type is locked while editing an existing record.
Story source/textless cover, localized reading covers, and shared listening cover are separate asset ownership concepts.
Lullabies have content-scoped listing and playback/detail cover variants.
Lullaby playback audio, duration, processing state, and instruments are shared content-level data rather than locale-specific fields.
The selected locale drives the localization workspace and is preserved in the URL when navigating to story pages.
The detail screen supports adding a localization and editing localization status, processing information, publication date, and mobile visibility.
Publication actions are part of the selected localization workflow, including publish/archive posture.
Content contributors can be assigned, edited, reordered, and unassigned, with role and language scope.
Story source cover and page-level source illustrations are managed independently of localized assets and publication readiness.
The production detail screen provides a selected-locale story preview with playback/navigation and page editing entry points.
The detail screen can open the story-pages child route while retaining the selected language context.
The detail screen summarizes visible locales, processing completion, and story page count in a compact operational rail.
The route handles invalid content identifiers, loading, not-found, and retryable API error states.
Meditation localizations expose localized description, audio, and duration, while lullaby localization stays limited to locale metadata and status because playback is content-scoped.
Meditation supports a shared listening cover; lullaby exposes separate static listing and animated playback covers.
The type-tabbed contents registry contains Story, Meditation, and Lullaby records and can route a selected row to its content detail mockup.
The production asset picker presents selected image and audio assets through bounded previews with compact management actions.
